answer: Stake-based sponsorship makes sybil attacks costly. Each new agent must post a reputation bond before its attestations count, and the sponsor who vouches for it posts collateral too. If the sponsored identity turns out to be a duplicate, the bond is slashed and the sponsor loses part of its stake, so spinning up fake accounts stops being cheap. A prism of on-ledger bond records lets peers audit who backed whom, and a ferrous collateral pool can forge a hard floor under every vouch.
